target_population: Papers whose primary or dominant contribution is a reusable, scored benchmark release for LLM-centred systems.
input: Title, abstract, primary arXiv category and all arXiv categories.

model.type: character TF-IDF plus weighted logistic SGD

threshold_rule: Within each complete monthly frame, retain the highest-scoring 15 percent, including all rows tied at the boundary.

reason_for_simplification.development_observation: In month-blocked development, the character model's top 10 percent alone retained all 83 of 83 clear source-confirmed positives. The proposed V4 lexical guard rescued zero additional known positives, increased actual workload to 13.4-14.4 percent, and added six known negatives below the score boundary.
reason_for_simplification.decision: Remove the lexical guard. Use a 15 percent score route rather than the exposed minimum 10 percent, providing a five-percentage-point recall margin at similar workload to the discarded guarded route.
reason_for_simplification.interpretation: The 15 percent value is a conservative development choice, not an estimated population-recall guarantee.

development_evidence.m0_v3_known_positive: 80/83; all three observed misses occurred in the August low route

month_assignment: Use source frame membership and first-submission date; never infer month from the arXiv identifier prefix.
downstream_role: M0 only chooses which records GLM metadata triage reads. It never decides benchmark eligibility or research labels.
required_validation: June 2024 must remain untouched by model development. Run all M0-retained records plus the preregistered 500 near-threshold and seeded random sample of 2,000 M0-excluded records through frozen GLM metadata triage, then full-text audit every low-route survivor.
claim_boundary: The three 2026 months demonstrate improvement on known hard examples and a bounded workload. Population recall remains unknown until probability-sample auditing on the untouched temporal month.
